name: Vascular Flow
description: Bidirectional transport intelligence in plant vasculature. Xylem carries water and minerals upward via transpiration pull; phloem distributes photosynthates downward via pressure-driven flow. Together they form a hydraulic computation network balancing supply and demand across the organism.

scope.definition: Velocity and efficiency of phloem sucrose transport — fraction of photosynthetically fixed carbon delivered to sink organs (roots, fruit) per unit time relative to source-to-sink distance, measured by radiolabeling.

evidence.source: Münch (1930) 'Die Stoffbewegungen in der Pflanze', Gustav Fischer; van Bel (2003) 'The phloem, a miracle of ingenuity', Plant, Cell & Environment 26:125-149.
cross_domain_examples: phloem transport velocity: 0.3-1.5 m/h for sucrose — delivers photosynthate to fruit 3 m distant within 2-6 hours
Münch pressure-flow model: osmotically-driven mass flow explains 0.91 of measured transport rates
companion cell-sieve element complex: ATP-driven sucrose loading achieves 10-50× concentration gradient vs mesophyll

scope.falsifiability: If radiotracer experiments show phloem transport velocity inconsistent with pressure-driven mass flow predictions, the Münch model requires modification.
scope.measurement_limits: Transport efficiency is temperature-dependent — cold slows phloem viscosity. Phloem exudate composition affects viscosity and thus flow rate. Long-distance transport (>10 m) requires intermediate unloading-loading steps in some species.
